name: The Pruyne and Kimberly partnership household
head: pruyne_peter

arrival.note: Kimberly's year is independently stated as 1832. Pruyne's own arrival is dated only by his shop - 'early in 1833' - and the household takes the earlier of the two because that is when it first existed in the town.

lives_at.note: Not attested for either man. Note that this is a BUSINESS household rather than a domestic one - see the research note.

works_at.note: The partnership is documented; that it was trading on 1 July 1835 specifically is the inference, since the retrospective sources do not supply a transaction on that exact day.

present_on_scene_date.note: Pruyne is married at Chicago on 20 August 1835, seven weeks after the scene date; Kimberly is continuously in the town's medical and public life through this period.

persons.name: Peter Pruyne

occupation.note: Early in 1833 Peter Pruyne and Edmund Stoughton Kimberly opened Chicago's second drug store.

persons.note: Andreas adds a dated domestic fact in a footnote: on August 20, 1835 Peter Pruyne married Rebecca, only daughter of Silas W. Sherman. That is seven weeks after the scene date, so on July 1 Rebecca Sherman is not silently added to this business household. FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Peter Pruyne,” (f1839_v0036, printed page 41, ward 1, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Pruyne' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins P. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 6 times, as “PRUYNE P”, “PRUYNE P AND CO”, “PRUYNE PETER”, 1833-10-22 to 1835-06-26: 2 federal land entries — E2SW sec 30 T39N R13E; W2NW sec 30 T39N R13E and 4 parcels of the school section — BL97 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; lot 1 of block 23 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 3 of block 119 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 8 of block 23 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), 171.10 acres stated in all, for $713.79 (ls0321, ls0322, ls0323, ls0324, ls0858, ls0859). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: PRUYNE P matches Peter Pruyne: the residents layer holds exactly one person of the surname and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

resident_research.evidence_for: Medical/pharmaceutical histories independently identify Peter Pruyne and Edmund Stoughton Kimberly as operators of Chicago's second drug store from early 1833. The business partnership strengthens Pruyne's profile but does not by itself establish a dwelling.

persons.name: Dr Edmund Stoughton Kimberly

birth_year.note: T-0478 replaces the age-at-death arithmetic with an explicit biographical date: Edmund Stoughton Kimberly was born at Troy, New York, April 7, 1803.

age_on_scene_date.note: Born April 7, 1803, so he was 32 on July 1, 1835.

occupation.note: Kimberly moved to Chicago in 1832, practiced medicine, and was the other half of the town's second drug store.

persons.note: T-0478 adds exact birth data and independent biography: born April 7, 1803 at Troy, New York; Union College graduate; medical training in New York; married Marie Theresa Ellis May 16, 1829; moved to Chicago in 1832. He was clerk of the August 5, 1833 incorporation meeting and one of the first town trustees. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Kimberly, Edmund S.” (tax_1833_057, line 109); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Kimberly, Dr. E. S.” (poll_1834_063, line 232). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Kimberly' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

resident_research.evidence_for: forenames agree initial for initial: entry 'Dr. E. S. Kimberly' against resident 'Dr Edmund Stoughton Kimberly'

research_note: A PARTNERSHIP RECORDED AS A HOUSEHOLD, WHICH IS A COMPROMISE AND IS FLAGGED AS ONE. Nothing says Pruyne and Kimberly shared a roof; what is documented is that they opened a shop together. They are grouped because the alternative - two single-person households, each pointing at the same building - would double the household count without adding a person, and because the schema's relationship vocabulary carries 'partner' precisely for this. ANY LATER USE THAT TREATS A HOUSEHOLD AS A DWELLING UNIT MUST READ THIS FIELD: lives_at is null here on purpose, and the household should not be given a dwelling by the inferred phase until the two men are separated. A NAME COLLISION KEPT SEPARATE: the W. Kimball who advertised dry goods at South Water and Clark in the Democrat of 26 November 1833 is a different trade and, on the evidence, a different man; he has his own household here.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.

address_later.note: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 prints this address against this person, in the entry quoted on the card: 'Pruyne, Peter, druggist and apothecary, South Water street'. It is evidence about 1839, written here as 1839's and read back onto no 1835 claim. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.

back_projection.note: NOT READ BACK, BECAUSE SOMETHING BETTER ALREADY STANDS. Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 prints an address against this name in 1839, and it is left where it is. An 1835 placement already stands: this household works at `pruyne_kimball_drugstore`, and clause 2 says an attested 1835 placement always beats a door printed 4 years later. The later address stays on the record as 1839's evidence and moves nothing.
